<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19133>

--- Comment #5 from Hugo Gruson (<mailto:hugo.gruson+Rbugzilla@normalesup.org|hugo.gruson+Rbugzilla@normalesup.org>) ---
Created attachment 3792
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3792&action=edit>
aperm special 2D case

Thanks for the helpful feedback!

I did run some benchmarks, but before covering the special cases with dimnames,
etc. and I think any potential gains were lost there.

I went back and wrote another patch (attached) directly in the C code as
suggested (+ 1 additional regression test). It's a nicer & more minimal patch
since all the input checking is already handled.

Here are the benchmarks, generated with the following code:

```
set.seed(20260819)

sizes <- c(1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7, 1e8, 1e9)

timings <- data.frame(
  size = sizes,
  user.self = numeric(length(sizes)),
  sys.self = numeric(length(sizes)),
  elapsed = numeric(length(sizes)),
  user.child = numeric(length(sizes)),
  sys.child = numeric(length(sizes))
)

for (i in seq_along(sizes)) {
  size <- sizes[i]
  m <- matrix(<http://sample.int|sample.int>(size), nrow = 10)
  timings[i, 2:6] <- aperm(m) |>
    system.time() |>
    replicate(n = 100) |>
    rowSums()
}
```


--- Comment #1 from Paul Murrell (<mailto:paul@stat.auckland.ac.nz|paul@stat.auckland.ac.nz>) ---
Can confirm segfaults.  Thanks for report!

However, the solution requires more surgery.

After the suggestion (5 -> 6), `x11("tiff:")` no longer segfaults, but
`x11("tiff::")` still does, as does `x11("jpeg::")`.

OTOH, `x11("png::")` does not and neither does `x11("bmp::")`.

A code comparison of those different cases might illuminate the problem.

Personally, I don't like the look of this ...
```
pp = strchr(tmp, ':'); *pp='\0';
```
... especially because `strchr()` is capable of returning a null pointer.
